about:
Sai Srikiran J is a student AI architect and aspiring entrepreneur who has independently
designed, built and shipped 10+ AI-powered applications, automation workflows and 6+
custom GPT agents. This document describes nine of them, each in plain language first
and then in technical detail.
Positioning: Generative AI, prompt engineering and SaaS product development. He moves
from market research and product strategy to hands-on implementation with React,
Python, Node.js and modern LLM APIs. He ranks in the top 200 global creators on
PromptBase, with 600+ business prompts sold.
Education: Integrated BBA (Business Analytics) + MBA (International Business) at the
Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT), 2025 to 2030. Before that, Class XII (Science) at
Somaiya School, CBSE, with 90.4%, and Class X at Atomic Energy Central School with
97%.

projects.title: Between the Tiers: three-tier architecture explainer
projects.body:
1. Between the Tiers: three-tier architecture explainer
Type: Interactive educational web page · Link: 3tierarchitecture.vercel.app
In plain terms. A single-page site that teaches how most web applications are split into
three jobs: showing information, applying business rules, and storing data. It was built for
Group-03's 20-minute talk in the Database Applications and Data Warehousing course at
IIFT Kakinada, and credits Hoffer, Ramesh & Topi's Modern Database Management as its
source. An online shop's "Place Order" button is the running example, and a short quiz
with a leaderboard lets visitors test what they learned.
Technical detail.
Content model: Each tier (Client, Application, Database) is shown with its
technologies and a sample snippet. The rule it teaches is that the client talks only to
the application tier, and the database talks only to the application tier.
Walkthrough: A scroll-driven "send the packet" interaction follows one Place Order
request through seven steps. The example logic checks stock and coupon validity,
computes the total with tax, and calls a PlaceOrder  stored procedure inside an ACID
transaction.
Quiz engine: Five questions, scored at 100 points per correct answer plus up to 50 for
speed. The leaderboard ranks by score, then total time.
Not verifiable from the page: the front-end framework and where leaderboard
scores are stored. Hosting is on Vercel.

projects.title: Urja Kaushal Learning Platform (UK-LMS)
projects.body:
2. Urja Kaushal Learning Platform (UK-LMS)
Type: Multilingual learning and livelihood platform prototype · Link: csrproject-
one.vercel.app
In plain terms. A prototype proposal for a Reliance Foundation CSR initiative that trains
rural communities in Jamnagar, Gujarat, in solar installation and related livelihoods. It
covers the whole path from enrolment to a certified job: learners take a 600-hour
programme, trainers and assessors record practical results, and certified learners are
matched to employers. The footer cites targets of 10 hubs, 6,000 beneficiaries, over 50%
women and 375 MWh a year of clean solar generation. The banner states that it is a
prototype using sample data only, not connected to any government or Reliance API. It
was built as a Team 5 proposal for IPM 2025-30.
Technical detail.
Roles: Nine demo roles open the matching interface in one click: learner, lab trainer,
mobilisation coordinator, external assessor, employer, programme manager, funder
(read-only impact view) and system administrator.

Access: Learners sign in with a mobile number and OTP. Staff and vendors use email.
Registration is a four-step flow.
Accessibility: The interface is Gujarati by default, with Hindi and English options, a
"listen" (text-to-speech style) button, and an online-mode indicator.
Admin and reporting functions shown in the role descriptions: question-bank
management, a certificate registry, audit logs, KPI tracking, and a risk register.
Stack: The site has routed pages ( /login , /register ) and is hosted on Vercel. The
framework and backend are not visible from the rendered pages.

projects.title: Cloud Transformation Decision Simulator
projects.body:
3. Cloud Transformation Decision Simulator
Type: Interactive board-proposal simulator · Link: decision-simulator
In plain terms. A web version of a board presentation for a fictional IT services firm, ABC
Technology Services, that wants to move from legacy IT services to an AI-enabled, data-
driven digital business. Instead of reading slides, a director can change the plan's levers
and watch the cost, payback and migration outcomes recalculate. The proposal asks the
board for a ₹25 Cr investment over 3 years (36 months, four stages from Assess to
Optimise), with migration in 3 waves under a 5Rs framework and four decisions needed on
the day. All figures are labelled illustrative.
Technical detail.
Simulator: Adjustable levers drive five live outputs: infrastructure cost, provisioning,
payback, share migrated by year 3, and staff certified by year 2. A "Reset to Board-
recommended plan" button restores the base case, and a "Compare scenarios" option
lets readers weigh alternative plans.
Calibration: The outputs are tuned so the recommended plan reproduces the deck's
stated figures, which keeps the simulator consistent with the proposal.
Assistant: An "Ask Jarvis" conversational helper answers questions about the
proposal. Its model and prompt design are not visible from the page.
Front end: A static page with in-page anchor navigation, headline stat cards and
technology tags (dev/test, Azure, AWS, data and AI, on-prem). It is hosted on GitHub
Pages. The calculation model itself is not shown on the rendered page.

projects.title: LEXIS: AI-Powered Policy Analyzer
projects.body:
4. LEXIS: AI-Powered Policy Analyzer
Type: AI web app for legal-document clarity · Link: lexis-policy-analyzer

In plain terms. LEXIS lets anyone paste a Terms & Conditions or Privacy Policy and get a
plain-English breakdown of what they are agreeing to, in under a minute. Its headline is
"Stop clicking Accept blindly." It flags risky clauses, gives an overall risk score, and lists
questions worth asking before agreeing. The footer states that it gives educational
summaries only and is not legal advice.
Technical detail.
Flow: The user pastes policy text or supplies a URL. The AI reads each clause,
classifies its risk level, and maps it to a plain-language meaning. The report then
shows a clause-by-clause breakdown, a risk score and key questions.
Two analysis modes: Consumer mode checks data rights and privacy tracking,
content ownership, account termination, auto-renewal traps and third-party data
sharing. Founder / Business mode checks IP ownership and licensing, liability caps and
indemnification, data processing agreements, AI-training clauses, and termination
and off-boarding.
Sample output: The landing page previews a finding with a category (such as Data
Collection), a risk badge (High Risk), a plain-language explanation and a "what this
means for you" line. A full analysis sits behind an "Unlock Full Analysis" button.
Front end: A static single-page app on GitHub Pages with animated statistics.

projects.title: SOP Builder for Teams
projects.body:
5. SOP Builder for Teams
Type: AI process-documentation web app · Link: standard-operating-procedures-builder
In plain terms. A tool that turns messy process knowledge, such as meeting notes, chat
transcripts or rough workflow outlines, into a clear standard operating procedure. A
paragraph like "every Monday Sarah pastes the weekly report into Slack, Jim reviews it by
noon" becomes a structured SOP with a purpose, named roles and numbered steps. The
pitch is that processes should not live in people's heads, where they are lost when
someone leaves.
Technical detail. The landing page lists six capabilities:
AI SOP generation: extracts roles, steps, decision points and exceptions from free-
form input.
Smart gap detection: flags unclear steps, missing roles and ambiguities for the author
to resolve.
Team enablement views: converts an SOP into a checklist, onboarding guide or
manager summary.

Role-specific output: filters an SOP to the steps one team member needs.
SOP library: a searchable home for documented processes.
Export and share: PDF, copy to clipboard and share link.
The workflow is four steps: paste input, AI builds the structure, review and refine inline,
then share. Use-case tabs cover operations, HR and onboarding, customer support,
agencies and startups. The page is a static site on GitHub Pages; the generation engine
behind the "Launch App" button is not visible from it.

projects.title: Lead Routing Bot
projects.body:
6. Lead Routing Bot
Type: RevOps simulator plus automation pack (GitHub repository) · Link: lead-routing-bot
In plain terms. A browser tool that shows how incoming sales leads can be scored and
sent to the right salesperson, so a revenue operations team can see and test its routing
logic. It is not a CRM replacement. Open one HTML file, load 15 sample leads, and see each
lead's score, qualification band, assigned rep and a draft outreach email. An
accompanying automation pack carries the same logic into real CRM stacks.
Technical detail.
Pipeline: normalise the lead, simulate enrichment, score fit (up to about 58 points)
and intent (up to about 52), apply disqualifier deductions, assign a band, route, create
a task with a response deadline, and draft outreach.
Bands and SLAs: Enterprise Priority (5 minutes), SQL (15 minutes), MQL (30 minutes),
Nurture (24 hours) and Disqualify.
Routing: twelve priority-ordered rules, covering existing owner, four territories, three
segments, two specialties, North American round robin and an exception queue.
Architecture: vanilla JavaScript organised under a single window.LRB  namespace
(validator, normaliser, enrichment, scoring, routing, generator, store, UI). The
namespace pattern was chosen because ES modules fail from file://  in Chrome.
Scoring weights, rules, reps and templates are JSON files, so behaviour changes
without code changes. State persists in localStorage, with light and dark themes, CSV
and JSON import, and an audit log.
Automation pack: JSON schemas, an n8n workflow blueprint, LLM prompts for
enrichment and outreach, and CRM payload examples for HubSpot and Salesforce,
with Slack notifications. The README describes these files; I could not open them to
verify their contents.

projects.title: Customer Support Automation (Support Reply Copilot)
projects.body:
7. Customer Support Automation (Support Reply Copilot)
Type: AI drafting tool with an n8n backend (GitHub repository) · Link: customer-support-
automation
In plain terms. Support Reply Copilot reads a pasted customer message, works out what
kind of issue it is and how urgent it is, and drafts a reply for a person to review. The design
principle is "AI suggests, human decides": nothing is sent automatically, and risky
messages such as billing or complaints are flagged with a "human review required"
banner. It is aimed at solo founders and support teams of 1 to 10 agents.
Technical detail.
Front end: a self-contained index.html  with no build step, using vanilla JavaScript, a
two-column layout, a four-state interface (empty, loading, error, results), form
validation, a 30-second timeout and a copy-to-clipboard button.
Inputs: customer message, business name, reply tone (friendly, professional or
empathetic), optional product context and internal knowledge-base notes.
Webhook contract: the page POSTs JSON to an n8n webhook ( support-copilot ).
The response holds a category (billing, bug, feature request, account issue, general
question or complaint), urgency, confidence, an internal summary, a draft reply, a next
step and a needs_human_review  flag.
Safe failure: if classification fails or returns invalid values, the workflow falls back to a
general-question category, low confidence, a holding reply and a forced human
review.
Backend: an importable n8n-workflow.json  (webhook, input normalisation, an LLM
call over HTTP, output validation and a response node). The repository's configuration
PDFs reference OpenRouter and Gemini as the model route. It also includes human-
review rules, a README and sample test tickets.

projects.title: Client Intelligence Agent
projects.body:
8. Client Intelligence Agent
Type: Multi-step AI research and outreach agent (GitHub repository) · Link: client-
intelligence
In plain terms. Give the agent a company name and it researches that company, then
produces a client briefing in which every claim is tied to a source, plus a reviewed
outreach email. A person must approve the email before anything can be sent. The

briefing includes a pitch outline, scope, discovery questions and the email. It only
proposes problems and offers that the user's own service line can actually address, and it
will not present a hypothesis as a fact in the email.
Technical detail.
Design principle: the model reads and writes, code makes the decisions, and a human
approves.
Architecture: a custom orchestrator with no agent framework, using a supervisor,
parallel researchers and a critic loop. Six research angles run in parallel: company
profile, news, sector, competitors, signals, and one specific to the user's service line.
Verification in code: a finding is kept only if its quote appears in the fetched text.
Quotes under five words are rejected, and every figure in a claim must appear in its
cited evidence. A critic then sends weak claims back, and the draft is revised until it
passes.
Sources: Wikipedia, Wikidata, the company's own site, live Google News headlines
(items older than 18 months dropped) and user-supplied documents, including PDFs.
Evidence is labelled "strong" or "headline-only".
Stack: Python 3.10+ with the standard library plus pypdf , and a plain HTML, CSS and
JavaScript front end with a live trace of the agent's steps. LLM backends are Gemini
(default), Claude via the Claude Code CLI (untested), a local Ollama model, and a
replay mode that runs recorded sessions with no network or API use.
Email: opt-in and off by default, over SMTP with a Gmail App password, explicit
confirmation, approved-only drafts and a demo mode that redirects everything to one
inbox.
Quality evidence: 32 deterministic unit tests, plus evals for grounding, fact recall and
hallucination traps. In a live Asian Paints run the critic rejected 3 of 8 claims in round
one, and the revised draft passed all 8. The README itself notes the small eval set
and the quota limits of the free Gemini tier.

projects.title: Document-to-Decision Agent (Accounts Payable)
projects.body:
9. Document-to-Decision Agent (Accounts Payable)
Type: Multi-step AI agent for finance operations (GitHub repository) · Link: document-to-
decision-agent
In plain terms. Finance teams check every invoice and contract by hand, and errors and
fraud slip through. This agent reads invoices and contracts (typed text, PDFs, scans or
phone photos), checks them against the company's vendor list and open purchase orders,

and decides to approve, send for review, or reject. Every exception goes to a person in an
exception queue. It does not pay anyone: it produces a payment file for a human to upload
to net banking or the ERP.
Technical detail.
Design principle: the model reads and writes, code decides every money question,
and a human approves. It is the companion to the Client Intelligence agent and shares
its core.
Pipeline: classify (keyword rules first, model only when ambiguous), extract (model,
in parallel, with an exact source quote per contract term), validate (code), decide
(code), draft messages (model), then the human queue.
Code-made checks: GSTIN format and checksum, CGST+SGST versus IGST by state,
valid GST slab, line and total arithmetic, future dates, exact and near duplicates across
batches, vendor master, bank-account change as a fraud signal, purchase-order
match on vendor, item, open quantity and price tolerance, approval limit, and contract
policy (payment terms, auto-renewal, liability, governing law, notice period). Any
critical issue means reject; any high or medium issue means review.
Memory and guardrails: state lives in SQLite. Ticking "Remember" waives a rule for
one vendor in later batches. Fraud and duplicate rejections cannot be overridden, an
unknown vendor is never waivable, and a bank-detail change creates an internal alert
to verify by phone.
Stack: Python 3.10+ (standard library, pypdf , fpdf2  for sample generation), a local
web server and UI, SQLite, and the same Gemini, Claude CLI, Ollama and replay
backends as its companion. Gemini vision is used for OCR of scans and photos, and
every OCR document is forced into human review.
Quality evidence: 43 deterministic tests that need no model. In the author's Gemini
evals (Nov 2026), 14 of 14 planted-error documents were decided correctly, including
as real PDFs, and 21 of 21 OCR fields were read correctly. The README cautions that
the sample documents are fictional and cleanly formatted, so these results are an
upper bound.
